title: Approve What, Exactly? Effect Binding and Trusted Rendering for Agent Step-Up Authorization
abstract: arXiv:2610.21063v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: AI agents now pause for approval before they send money, delete files or email outsiders, and that approval is usually treated as a second factor. We argue it is one only when compromising the agent cannot produce it and when it names exactly what it approves, and we test both conditions. We define twelve attacks on the approval path, including decoy recipients, amount cancellation, card padding, label spoofing, enrollment squatting and threshold splitting, and run them against the Agent Payments Protocol (AP2), the Microsoft action-bound approval design and Model Context Protocol (MCP) elicitation. An audit of ten agent runtimes finds no third-party verifiable approval record, no flood limits where measurable, and post-approval argument changes in four of eight runtimes with measurable binding. As a reference defense we build ASU (Agent Step-Up), a gateway that renders the approval card from a canonical effect descriptor, has a passke

translated_title: 批准的究竟是什么？面向智能体升格授权的效果绑定与可信渲染
translated_abstract: AI智能体如今在发送资金、删除文件或向外部发送邮件之前会暂停等待人工批准，而这种批准通常被视为第二认证因素。我们认为，只有当攻破智能体本身无法产生该批准、且批准内容明确指出了其所批准的具体操作时，它才真正构成第二因素，并对这两个条件进行了检验。我们定义了针对批准路径的十二种攻击，包括诱饵收件人、金额取消、卡片填充、标签伪造、注册抢占和阈值拆分，并对Agent Payments Protocol（AP2）、微软的动作绑定批准设计以及Model Context Protocol（MCP）的引导机制进行了测试。对十个智能体运行时的审计发现：不存在第三方可验证的批准记录，在可测量的情况下缺乏洪泛限制，并且在八个具有可测量绑定的运行时中有四个存在批准后参数被篡改的情况。作为参考防御方案，我们构建了ASU（Agent Step-Up），一个从规范化效果描述符渲染批准卡片、并采用通行密钥（passkey）……（摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文指出智能体人工批准只有在“攻破智能体无法伪造”且“精确指明所批准操作”时才构成真正的第二因素，定义了十二种批准路径攻击并测试了AP2、微软方案与MCP的缺陷，同时提出基于规范化效果描述符与可信渲染的参考防御网关ASU。
